purpose: The declared negative cases for the read-only PGM-01 compatibility view. Every fixture is ONE named edit to a real retained record, so a reader can tell a found record from a constructed one without reading a diff.

source.serialization: json.dumps(document, indent=2) + two newlines, which reproduces the source bytes exactly

why_derived: The ten retained PGM-01 records in this repository are all v1 and carry only pass, skipped, and inconclusive. There is no failed, unavailable, not-computed, malformed, unsupported, or tampered record anywhere in the history, so each of those cases is constructed from real bytes by a single named edit rather than written from imagination.

cases.why: A failed legacy check maps to failed and stays failed; it is not rounded to an error or dropped.
Unavailable is neither passed nor failed. A check that could not run is not a check that ran and failed, and the mapping keeps them apart.
PGM-01 v1 has no not-computed status. The mapping refuses the record rather than inventing a translation for a state the schema never had, and that refusal is the expected result, not a defect.

The classic tamper: an inconclusive check edited to read as a pass, presented under the digest of the record it was made from. Binding the expected digest is what turns it from a readable record into a refused one, and no field of the altered source is interpreted.
An unknown schema major is refused rather than guessed at, read as empty, or reinterpreted as the current one.

derivation.to: an implementation name, not an object

cases.why: A record that declares the right schema and does not have its shape is malformed, not empty. The mapping reports which field is wrong instead of skipping it.
Bytes that are not JSON are unreadable. No legacy field is interpreted and nothing is recovered from the prefix that did parse.

A real retained file, read as itself. The append-only correction is a quire.evidence-correction/v1 record, not a PGM-01 evidence record, and the mapping refuses to read it as one rather than mapping whichever fields happen to overlap.
